key_insight: Solphin is a Python toolkit that streamlines photovoltaic efficiency analysis for bulk materials computed with DFT, helping researchers estimate solar-cell potential more easily and reproducibly.
engineering_relevance: It lowers the barrier to screening and optimizing candidate photovoltaic materials by automating post-processing and efficiency metrics used in device-oriented materials discovery.
method: Generates and post-processes photovoltaic calculations from periodic solid-state DFT
Computes photovoltaic Figure of Merit, detailed balance, and spectroscopic limited maximum efficiency
Provides a user-friendly Python workflow for reproducible materials analysis
evidence_signal: The paper presents Solphin as a software package and evaluates its utility through the photovoltaic metrics it can compute, rather than reporting a new experimental dataset.
watch_item: As a post-processing tool, results will depend on the quality and assumptions of the underlying DFT inputs and efficiency models.
paper_title: Solphin: Photovoltaic efficiency analysis for bulk materials using Python
